events.summary: China and Sri Lanka agreed to promote Port City and Hambantota projects.
IMF initially approved a US$337 million payout for Sri Lanka.
IMF initially approved a $337 million payout pending further debt restructuring progress.
China pledged assistance for Katunayake Airport, Hambantota Port and Colombo Port City development.
ADB and Sri Lanka signed a $100 million SME finance and guarantee loan.
Cabinet approved seeking proposals to promote Sri Lankan-flag ship registration.
Cabinet paper planned to reduce agricultural electricity charges for Northern farmers.
Government approved transferring expressway operations and assets to Sahasya Investment Limited.
Cabinet approved digitising the entire foreign employment sector.
Cargills and USAID launched solar-supported EV charging stations in Colombo.
Japan promised to resume suspended Sri Lankan development projects after creditor agreement
Japan extended UNDP-mediated financial aid for Sri Lanka anti-corruption efforts
Cabinet approved digitisation of Sri Lanka’s foreign employment sector
IMF staff-level agreement could unlock the next EFF financing tranche.
India formalised an additional grant for houses and infrastructure in Sobitha Thero Village.
ADB launched its 2024–2028 country partnership strategy for Sri Lanka.
India agreed to fund full development of Kankesanturai Port.
President unveiled an initiative for sustainable development across the tropical belt.
Sri Lanka and Chongqing signed a sister-district agreement involving Kalutara.
Sri Lanka signed agreements with 33 Chinese vocational training institutes.
Three Gorges Institute planned a Sri Lankan branch for vocational training.
India pledged a grant to develop Kankesanthurai Port in Jaffna.
Construction of a new KKS port terminal was underway.
Cabinet approved procurement to import 42 million eggs for market stabilisation.
Japan signed grant assistance covering marine, fishing, health and vocational training needs.
CEB introduced installment payments for new electricity connections.
ADB approved a loan expanding SME finance access and resilience in Sri Lanka.
UNDP and partners inaugurated a mobile women’s empowerment exhibition in Jaffna.
Fourteen investors expressed interest in divesting Sri Lanka’s state-owned Litro Gas companies.
President ordered Rs. 500 million allocation for nationwide paddy purchases.
Cabinet approved signing Japan’s grant for humanitarian and state-sector support.
CEB estimates renewable energy infrastructure investment required through 2030.
Four additional DP Education IT campuses are being established in Northern Province.
Government allocated funds to settle farmers’ fertilizer credit arrears.
CEB approved an instalment scheme for new electricity connection charges.
Cabinet increased the school meal allocation to Rs. 110 per meal.
Save the Children pledged three food items for 200,000 students.
Cabinet extended the electric vehicle import scheme validity period.
Cabinet approved inviting investors for Galle Harbour commercial and recreation development.
Cabinet approved Rs. 110 meals for primary students under the 2024 school food programme.
Save the Children agreed to provide food to 200,000 students in 917 schools.
India provided advance aid for Sri Lanka’s unique identity card project.
BOI signed an $8 million agreement for an export bedding manufacturing venture.
District committee rejected approval for proposed Samanalawewa mini hydro project.
Sri Lanka and India signed agreement for hybrid renewable energy systems on three Jaffna islands.
Finance Ministry unveiled governance action plan based on IMF diagnostic recommendations.
